client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: A facility uses germicidal ultraviolet (UV) irradiation as a no-touch disinfection technology for rooms of clients with Candida auris. Which practice aligns with CDC guidance?

options.A: Use UV only as a supplement to standard environmental cleaning and disinfection
options.B: Replace standard manual cleaning and disinfection with UV irradiation
options.C: Use UV before removing visible soil and omit routine surface disinfection
options.D: Assume UV parameters are fully standardized and effective for every room configuration

rationale: CDC states that data on no-touch devices such as germicidal UV irradiation for C. auris are limited and that the parameters required for effective disinfection are not yet well understood. CDC therefore recommends using these methods only as a supplement to standard cleaning and disinfection methods. A is correct. B and C improperly replace core environmental cleaning, while D overstates the certainty and standardization of UV effectiveness.
educational_objective: Use germicidal UV irradiation as an adjunct—not a replacement—for standard environmental cleaning and disinfection when applying CDC guidance for C. auris rooms.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Section 'Surface disinfectants' > 'No-touch devices': data on germicidal UV irradiation and vaporized hydrogen peroxide are limited; these methods should only supplement standard cleaning and disinfection methods
source_claim_supported: Germicidal UV irradiation for C. auris should be used only as a supplement to standard cleaning and disinfection because effectiveness data and required parameters remain limited.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8 / PDF p.12: 'Apply principles of infection prevention,' 'Facilitate appropriate and safe use of equipment,' and 'Assess client care environment'; Appendix A printed pp.25-26 / PDF pp.29-30, Safe Use of Equipment and Standard Precautions/Transmission-Based Precautions/Surgical Asepsis
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — environmental disinfection technology
correction_summary: The original generic claim that UV technology provides established additional pathogen reduction after terminal cleaning was too broad for a universal item. Reframed the scenario to C. auris, for which current CDC guidance explicitly states that no-touch UV devices have limited evidence and should be used only as a supplement to standard cleaning and disinfection.
audit_findings: A directly matches current CDC C. auris guidance. B and C replace required standard cleaning/disinfection, and D contradicts CDC's statement that effective parameters are not yet well understood. The corrected item avoids claiming a universal quantitative pathogen-reduction benefit. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
